learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will identify and use coordinating, subordinating, and correlative conjunctions to build complex and compound sentences smoothly.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Writing short sentences is easy. But writing long, beautiful, flowing sentences requires strong glue! Conjunctions and linking words are the super-glue of grammar. Let's learn how to stick complex ideas together perfectly.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: These join words or independent clauses that are equally important. An easy way to remember them is the acronym FANBOYS: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So.
examples_or_templates: I was tired, **so** I went to sleep.
She is small, **yet** she is very strong.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: These join a dependent clause (which can't stand alone) to a main independent clause. They often show a relationship of time, reason, or condition.
examples_or_templates: Reason: We stayed inside **because** it was raining.
Condition: You cannot watch TV **unless** you finish your homework.
Time: I will call you **when** I arrive.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: These are 'teamwork' conjunctions that always come in pairs. They connect two balanced clauses, phrases, or words.
examples_or_templates: **Either** you clean your room, **or** you cannot go out.
She is **not only** smart **but also** very kind.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which of the following is a Coordinating Conjunction (from FANBOYS)?
❓ Complete the Correlative pair: 'I will eat _____ the apple _____ the orange.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Join these two sentences using a Subordinating Conjunction: 'It was raining heavily. We went to school.'
subjective_practice.hint: Use a word that shows contrast, like 'Although' or 'Even though'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with a FANBOYS conjunction: 'I wanted to buy a new game, _____ I didn't have enough money.'
✍️ Write a sentence using the pair 'Not only ... but also'.
subjective_practice.hint: Think of someone who has two great qualities (e.g., talented and hardworking).

activity_or_assignment.title: 🚂 The Sentence Train
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write down three very short sentences. Example: 'I woke up. I brushed my teeth. I was late.' Now, use your conjunctions (like 'After', 'and', 'because') to combine them into one single, flowing sentence!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS) join equal parts of a sentence.
⭐ Subordinating conjunctions (because, although, if) join a dependent clause to a main clause.
⭐ Correlative conjunctions work in pairs (either/or, neither/nor, not only/but also).
